reviews.text: What we end up with is an almost entirely forgettable werewolf outing that had something it wanted to say, but was entirely too late to do it.
reviews.author: Jeff Beck

reviews.text: ... a film that grows on you as you are watching it.
reviews.author: Emilie Black

reviews.text: The Beast Within is a deeply distressing portrayal of generational trauma through the eyes of Little Red Riding Hood.
reviews.author: Ygraine Hackett-Cantabrana

reviews.text: At its heart, this patient and measured horror thriller has human interests that stretch well beyond genre. Father-daughter relationships, loss of innocence, and generational trauma are just some of the thematic through-lines.
reviews.author: Keith Garlington

reviews.text: A clunky and irritatingly dull domestic abuse drama masquerading as a werewolf film, The Beast Within is too unsophisticated in its approach and ultimately insincere in its explorations of trauma.
reviews.author: Nicholas Bell

reviews.text: Though chillingly atmospheric, there's not much of a story.
reviews.author: Dennis Schwartz

reviews.text: Lycanthropy as a family secret.
reviews.author: Abbie Bernstein

reviews.text: It's certainly possible to pull off a fresh take on the werewolf formula, but this movie doesn't quite make it; it's atmospheric, to be sure but also slow-paced and lacking in surprises or scares.
reviews.author: Jeffrey M. Anderson

reviews.text: There are so many issues in orbit around domestic violence–the danger of staying, the danger of running, the way violence might pass on generationally–that are portrayed without due consideration...
reviews.author: Walter Chaw

reviews.text: The Beast Within isn’t a terrible film, but sadly it is not a particularly great one either, so ham-fisted is its approach to its central themes.
reviews.author: Alexandra Heller-Nicholas

reviews.text: The Beast Within yearns to be more than a small-scale monster horror flick, desiring to explore challenging, interesting ideas about identity, family, and even free will.
reviews.author: Brandon Lewis

reviews.text: The characters here are pretty flat, and the saving grace could have been the internal struggle of “good wolf” vs. “bad wolf” that the film promises Noah to go through. You never get any sense that Noah is a good man.
reviews.author: Sara Clements

reviews.text: Kit Harington reviles as a monster inside and out in a poorly executed allegory of domestic abuse. The Beast Within's double entendre has poetic intent but doesn't fill the common sense void in a flawed narrative.
reviews.author: Julian Roman

reviews.text: If you excised the film’s brief prologue and the film’s final few minutes, you’d have a straightforward, reasonably powerful family melodrama. Which reminds us what a problem it is that this is supposed to be a horror movie.
reviews.author: Daniel Gorman

reviews.text: The film prioritizes an unsettling ambiance and strong performances over a high body count and full-on creature reveal. It’s worthwhile if you enjoy a slow burn but may leave those hankering for straightforward bloody horror hungry and drooling for more.
reviews.author: Chris Sawin

reviews.text: The polished craft contributions and solid cast help to round out a tight production package. But it’s one built around a concept that doesn’t entirely work in the end.
reviews.author: Jordan Mintzer

reviews.text: The actual ideas that might lift this above ordinary genre fare fall short, while the vivid tension and anxious character identification needed to excel on a humbler plane never quite arrive.
reviews.author: Dennis Harvey

reviews.text: There’s no sense of life being lived within the world of the film, which is indicated by a general refusal to shade in any details about the environment or even the characters beyond their scene-by-scene purpose.
reviews.author: Vikram Murthi

reviews.text: This slow-burning British psychological thriller struggles to build consistent suspense to match its atmospheric visuals.
reviews.author: Todd Jorgenson

reviews.text: Whilst the film could certainly do with tightening up the pace or exploring its themes more deeply, it works well as a character study.
reviews.author: Jennie Kermode

reviews.text: It's hampered by the tiny scope of its blatantly obvious metaphor bludgeoned into the viewer five minutes in
reviews.author: Robert Kojder

reviews.text: Director Alexander J. Farrell imbues The Beast Within with a creative take on werewolf lore, and despite the rather middling first hour, still warrants a watch to truly appreciate the final act’s commitment to its fascinating and thrilling ideology.
reviews.author: Aaron Peterson

reviews.text: A poignant horror fairy tale that’s at its strongest when exploring the psychological fallout, but it’s one that struggles to seamlessly blend the Gothic fantasy with authentic coming-of-age drama.
reviews.author: Meagan Navarro

reviews.text: The visual scheme feels better thought through than the narrative approach to the movie’s themes; the final moments make it clear what the filmmakers are trying to say, even as they further muddle the way in which they’re saying it.
reviews.author: Michael Gingold

reviews.text: Despite having an interesting take on werewolves, The Beast Within proves to be a middling experience.
reviews.author: Kenneth Seward Jr.

reviews.text: [W]e're left with something that feels like a cheap allegory.
reviews.author: Mark Dujsik

reviews.text: The Beast Within is an artistry in how a film can captivate an audience through suspense and their own imagination, rather than visually stuffing them with jump scares and gore. The Beast Within is a suspenseful showcase, and well worth watching.
reviews.author: Romey Norton

reviews.text: Concentrating far more on mood than storytelling, the movie ends up being an exercise in stagnation.
reviews.author: Charles Koplinski

reviews.text: A psychological horror film that offers rewards for viewers who are willing to be patient with the slow-and-steady pace.
reviews.author: Mike McGranaghan

reviews.text: A fairly lackluster and highly unoriginal addition to the werewolf subgenre of horror, The Beast Within has so much potential, on which it just never fully delivers.
reviews.author: Edward Douglas

reviews.text: The Beast Within is a supernaturally laced thriller, but seems as if came from a painful, dark personal place where the horrors are human and the wounds remain open forever.
reviews.author: Randy Myers

reviews.text: The Beast Within earns the distinction of being the most uneventful werewolf movie I've seen.
reviews.author: Joseph Robinson

reviews.text: Alexander J. Farrell takes an impressive first step with a production rich with gothic references, even if the tension & suspense evaporate quickly.
reviews.author: Ferdosa Abdi

reviews.text: With its dreamlike visuals and strong performances, this is a striking modern fairytale.
reviews.author: Nikki Baughan

reviews.text: Kit Harington gets hairy but his werewolf movie is hoary, as what passes for atmospheric horror is simply a tired, turgid retread of scareflick tropes.
reviews.author: Christopher Lloyd

reviews.text: Gritty, but shallow, unimaginative and underwhelming.
reviews.author: Avi Offer

reviews.text: Has mood and competent performances, but there’s very little to the production that’s meant to grab the viewer, often caught struggling to find intensity with a tale of growing threat.
reviews.author: Brian Orndorf

reviews.text: The Beast Within tells a tragically human story of abuse and survival disguised in lycanthropic fairytale clothing.
reviews.author: Molly Henery

reviews.text: [In THE BEAST WITHIN]...a werewolf curse adds an additional layer to this vicious domestic cycle that is doomed to repeat itself until the curse breaks.
reviews.author: Sarah Musnicky

reviews.text: He's a monster all right, but exactly what kind of monster feels loosely examined here through a vague genre exercise ... until it's suddenly made more explicit in ham-fisted ways.
reviews.author: Robert Taylor

reviews.text: ... all the tension, all the prolonged silences, and even the culminating final confrontation lacks any tension or mystery for we can pierce the veil of the cinematic illusion and recognize the beast within.
reviews.author: Douglas Davidson

reviews.text: This is by far and away the tensest of slow burns. Seek it out if you want to see a deeply atmospheric family drama.
reviews.author: Benjamin Franz

synopsis: After a series of strange events leads her to question her family's isolated life on a fortified compound deep in the English wilds, 10-year-old Willow follows her parents on one of their secret late-night treks to the heart of the ancient forest. But upon witnessing her father undergo a terrible transformation, she too becomes ensnared by the dark ancestral secret they've tried so desperately to conceal.
